status: PROPOSAL SLATE ONLY — not preregistration, not an assigned lane, not validation
scope: Three geological hypotheses distinct in mechanism from the implemented repository candidates. Rank is research-priority order, not predicted competition rank or score.
lane_note: The current request does not identify the single assigned method paragraph required by the standing protocol. A33-R7 is exhausted at 3/3. This slate does not authorize a holdout experiment or a competition slot.
ranking_basis: Qualitative hidden-fault plausibility, novelty relative to local implementations, source risk, and implementation cost. No numeric DTI or leaderboard projection is made. Any future number must be HOLDOUT-DTI with evaluator version, withheld-positive count, and 95% CI, or ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED from a submission-page receipt.

hypotheses.title: Fault-guided aqueous-geochemistry mixing fronts
layers: Official INGENIOUS GDR #1391 well/spring aqueous-geochemistry records, if raw analyte fields are present after a source-schema audit
GeoDAWN magnetic/gravity edge and conductivity context only after official/mirror provenance and common support are documented
No catalogue distance, fault-derived attribute, or thermalclass field may enter as a predictor
hypotheses.physical_signature: After mapping the actual source schema, transform eligible aqueous analytes with predeclared compositional log-ratios or endmember distances; test for spatially coherent mixing-front changes aligned with independent geophysical lineaments. Do not assume any particular ion or ratio exists until the GDB is inspected.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_catalogue_missing_faults: Deep, permeable faults can mix hydrothermal and shallow groundwater endmembers and feed springs or wells without a mapped Quaternary surface trace. A chemistry transition may therefore reveal a fluid conduit where the catalogue has no trace, but it cannot establish a fault by itself.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo_prior_art: Local `gdr_wellspring_in_footprint.csv` retains temperature, thermal class and quartz/chalcedony/cation geothermometers; H35/H38 and prior CSHT/PALEOTEMP concepts use thermal/geothermometer or spring-proximity evidence. No implemented candidate uses audited raw aqueous-ion mixing fronts. The local CSV has no raw major/minor-ion columns and contains `dist_known_fault_px`, which is catalogue-derived leakage and must be excluded.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Evaporite dissolution, lithology-controlled groundwater chemistry, or a shallow aquifer boundary unrelated to a fault.
hypotheses.expected_rank: 1 — highest research priority in this proposal slate only; expected leaderboard rank/score is not estimable.
hypotheses.expected_qualitative_holdout_potential: Potentially medium-to-high mechanism relevance, but sign and utility are unknown; sparse/repeated point sampling and non-fault hydrochemistry may dominate.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium after source access; high uncertainty. Requires GDB schema/CRS/license audit, repeated-record deduplication, point-support treatment, analyte missingness checks, spatially blocked feature-alone canaries, and matched non-fault controls.

required_official_sources.availability: Official listing is public under CC BY 4.0 and lists a 19.85 MB GDB, but direct asset retrieval returned HTTP 500; no official bytes/schema were obtained.

hypotheses.block_reason: Required official chemistry payload not locally obtainable/verified in this review; the community-mirror CSV is not a chemistry substitute and exposes a catalogue-distance leakage field.

hypotheses.title: Depth-persistent magnetotelluric conductance walls
layers: USGS Great Basin electrical-conductance maps at 2–12, 12–20, 20–50, 50–90 and 90–200 km depth (actual layer support and resolution to be checked)
Potential-field/contact context only where grid and scale are compatible; no upsampling treated as new 100 m information
hypotheses.physical_signature: Measure whether a lateral conductance edge or wall persists across the crustal depth intervals and whether its orientation is compatible with independently resolved magnetic/gravity lineaments. Keep the 2–12 km map separate from deeper regional conductance; do not convert broad regional gradients into 100 m fault traces.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_catalogue_missing_faults: A buried permeable structure or altered fault zone may create a subsurface conductive contrast beneath basin cover even when no surface fault trace is mapped. Cross-depth persistence could distinguish a deep structure from a shallow saline layer, subject to model resolution.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo_prior_art: The local stack has a single owner-mirror `cond_surf` channel, while H33-R3-4 previously proposed MT phase-tensor skew from transfer functions. This proposal uses depth-interval conductance-map persistence, not phase-tensor skew or the existing single-surface-conductivity blend; it is adjacent MT prior art and requires explicit overlap review.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Regional conductive basin fill, saline groundwater, or a deep conductive lithologic/shear zone that is not a fault relevant to the target.
hypotheses.expected_rank: 2 — second research priority in this proposal slate only; expected leaderboard rank/score is not estimable.
hypotheses.expected_qualitative_holdout_potential: Moderate conceptual upside for blind structures, discounted for coarse/inversion-smoothed map resolution and broad non-fault conductivity contrasts.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high. Requires retrieving and hashing the five USGS layers, inspecting CRS/grid/uncertainty and spatial resolution, aligning them without false 100 m precision, and testing each layer alone before any joint score.

required_official_sources.availability: Official metadata and five layer names verified; payloads, terms, target coverage, and grid support have not been audited.

hypotheses.block_reason: The official record is accessible, but no layer payload, target-grid coverage, licensing terms, or edge-scale resolution was verified from local bytes.

hypotheses.title: Cross-catchment channel-profile knickpoints and deflection alignments
layers: USGS 3DEP 1 m bare-earth DEM tiles on the exact finite template footprint
Derived flow paths, longitudinal channel profiles, local slope/curvature breaks, and cross-catchment orientation consistency
Optional GeoDAWN edge context only after official payload/provenance and scale compatibility are checked
hypotheses.physical_signature: Detect prespecified channel-profile slope breaks and lateral deflections that recur along a common lineament across separate catchments; compare channel-bank and profile evidence to local terrain controls rather than treating every linear step as a fault.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_catalogue_missing_faults: Subtle young or poorly mapped faults can locally offset drainage, create profile knickpoints, or align channel deflections without a trace in the regional catalogue. This is most relevant to weakly expressed structures; fully blind faults with no geomorphic response are outside its sensitivity.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo_prior_art: Existing 12-band LiDAR summaries and H33-R3-1/DPPS characterize 100 m scarp steps, relief, coherence, and line-integrated scarps. No local implementation tests longitudinal channel-profile discontinuities and cross-catchment drainage-network topology from raw 1 m DEMs.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic knickpoints, Lake Lahontan shoreline/terrace risers, erosional base-level changes, roads, dams, or drainage engineering.
hypotheses.expected_rank: 3 — third research priority in this proposal slate only; expected leaderboard rank/score is not estimable.
hypotheses.expected_qualitative_holdout_potential: Low-to-moderate for catalogue-missing faults: fine topography helps where expression exists, but erosion and shoreline geomorphology are strong competing explanations.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: large multi-tile raw DEM staging, vertical/datum/collection seam audit, hydrologic conditioning, stream extraction, spatial blocking, and per-feature leakage canaries.

required_official_sources.availability: Official page confirms free/no-use-restriction products; TNM API returned downloadable 1 m GeoTIFF tile records at two finite-template sample locations. Sample raw tiles were not downloaded, hashes and complete footprint coverage are not established.

hypotheses.block_reason: Catalog-level availability passed only at two sampled in-footprint locations; the raw DEM files are not staged, full coverage and tile continuity are unverified, and the current task supplies no authorized method lane.
